clue.text: See 30
Error cut out electronic circuits

indicators.note: to cut something out is to remove it, so the electronic letter is dropped from the error word

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or error
E is the standard abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A mistake has removed some electronic circuitry from a device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circuits' looks like part of the electronics picture, but it is the definition, in the sense of laps of a track.
explanation.definitionFit: Laps are complete circuits of a racetrack or swimming pool.

clue.text: Poet quavers if I erase extract

indicators.note: an extract is a passage taken from a longer text, so the letters are lifted from inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A poet trembles as he deletes a passage from his work.
explanation.definitionFit: A versifier is a writer of verse, often a modest or mechanical one, so a kind of poet.

clue.text: Fertile land's fit for Middle Eastern nations

parts.note: arable describes land fit for ploughing and crops, with the 's read as 'has'
an ague is a fit of fever and shivering

explanation.surface: Productive farmland is suitable for the countries of the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit for' reads as one phrase meaning suitable; split it, as 'fit' is the shivering fit and 'for' only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arab League is the regional organisation of Arab states, many of them in the Middle East.

clue.text: A song of praise is almost found, when engineers are gathered round?

definitions.text: A song of praise is almost found, when engineers are gathered round?

indicators.note: people gathered round something surround it, so the engineers enclose the shortened song

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: a hymn is a song praising God

explanation.surface: A hymn of sorts emerges when a group of engineers gather in a circle to sing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and a teasing description: a near-hymn inside RE gives a piece of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhyme is a short verse or song, so a near-hymn surrounded by singers loosely describes one.

clue.text: Attacks place of vice and beauty

parts.note: to bomb a target is to attack it
hell is the place of wickedness and punishment

explanation.surface: Someone launches assaults on a den of iniquity and on loveliness alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombshell is slang for a strikingly attractive woman, a great beauty.

clue.text: Head of bid's going to accept American client eventually

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so the shortened bid holds the American letters
the head of a word is its first letter, which is the one taken away
a letter going is one that leaves the word

parts.note: a tender is a formal bid for a contract
US is short for American, the United States

explanation.surface: A bidding firm's leader leaves, taking on an American who will become a client.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of bid' looks like the letter B; instead the bid is TENDER, whose head T goes, leaving ENDER to take in US.
explanation.definitionFit: The end user is the person who finally uses a product, the customer at the end of the chain.

clue.text: Alias Smith and Jones broadcast?

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so the word for these men is taken by its sound

parts.note: Smith and Jones are ordinary men's surnames, so two guys

explanation.surface: A TV programme about the outlaws known by the alias Smith and Jones.
explanation.walkthrough: Alias Smith and Jones was a western TV series about two outlaws using false names; here the names just stand for two ordinary guys.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an outward appearance or assumed identity, much like an alias.

clue.text: English and American workers chewed flesh out

parts.note: labor, in the American spelling, means the workforce collectively
chewed food is food that was eaten, so ate

explanation.surface: An English and American workforce gnawed meat off the bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chewed flesh' reads as one picture; the definition is the phrasal verb 'flesh out'.
explanation.definitionFit: To flesh out a plan is to add detail to it, which is to expand on or develop it.

clue.text: What happens if Macron declares Frexit, going AWOL?

definitions.text: What happens if Macron declares Frexit, going AWOL?

parts.words: What happens if Macron declares Frexit, going AWOL?
parts.note: a ... president announcing France's exit would literally be a ... departure, and absence without permission is the idiom's meaning

explanation.walkthrough: Frexit is a coined word for France leaving the European Union, after Brexit; the clue reads the idiom literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names leaving without permission or without saying goodbye, the very thing going AWOL describes.

clue.text: Depict harbour fish

parts.note: a port is a harbour for ships
a ray is a flat sea fish

explanation.surface: An artist is asked to paint fish in a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray something is to represent it in a picture or in words, a synonym of depict.

clue.text: Wine produced by armed group formerly

parts.note: something produced has been made
the IRA, the Irish Republican Army, was a paramilitary group that has since laid down its arms

explanation.surface: A wine that was once made by paramilitaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a fortified wine from the Portuguese Atlantic island of that name.

clue.text: Supporters surrounding United scouts

indicators.note: surrounding means enclosing, so the supporters go round the word for united

parts.note: piers are pillars that support a bridge or building
things united are made one

explanation.surface: Football fans gather around Manchester United's talent spotters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporters' and 'United' suggest football fans; here they are piers holding up a structure and ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouts go ahead to explore unknown ground, as pioneers do in opening up new territory.

clue.text: Look after return of deodorised baby shoes?

indicators.note: a return is a journey back, so the remaining letters are read from right to left
deodorising removes body odour, BO, so those two letters are taken out

parts.note: bootees are knitted woollen shoes for babies

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to deal with a baby's smelly shoes coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: BO is body odour; removing it from BOOTEES leaves OTEES, which reads backwards as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To see to a task is to deal with it or take care of it, a phrase meaning look after.

clue.text: 51 in pilgrimage returning to river in San Quentin?

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the combined letters are read in reverse
one thing in another sits inside it, so the Roman numeral goes into the pilgrimage word

parts.note: the hajj, also spelt haj, is the Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca
LI is 51 in Roman numerals
the Ouse is a river, in fact several, in England

explanation.surface: A pilgrim travels back to the river near a famous prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' acts on the whole container, giving JAILH; the hajj is the Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca, and the Ouse is an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: San Quentin is a well-known Californian prison, an example of a jailhouse, hence the question mark.

clue.text: The French tucking into roly-poly jam puds for starters

indicators.note: the French article tucks itself inside the scrambled pudding letters
roly-poly suggests rolling over and over, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

parts.note: le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: French diners eat roly-poly and jam puddings as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: Roly-poly is a British suet pudding rolled with jam; 'starters' looks like a first course but means devices that start cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Jump leads are the cables used to start a car with a flat battery from another car.

clue.text: Released, one in Cote d'Ivoire perhaps took charge after takeover

indicators.note: after places the leading word behind the takeover word

parts.note: un is French for one, French being the official language of Ivory Coast
a coup is a sudden seizure of power
someone who took charge led

explanation.surface: A man in Ivory Coast was freed after a coup in which someone seized command.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncouple is to disconnect, so something uncoupled has been detached or set free.

clue.text: Cater in mess for processed food outlets

indicators.note: letters in a mess are jumbled up, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: Provide meals in an army mess hall for fast-food chains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Processed food outlets' looks like takeaways; in fact it is a lavatorial description of the rectum.
explanation.definitionFit: The recta are the final sections of the bowel, through which digested food leaves the body.

clue.text: Mark of quality

definitions.meaning: a written mark or symbol, such as a letter of an alphabet
a distinctive trait or the moral strength of a person

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase, 'Mark of quality' looks like a hallmark; split it into two senses joined by 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A character is both a written sign and a person's distinguishing nature or strength.

clue.text: Desert island east of French waters and west of Thailand

indicators.note: in an across entry east is to the right, so the island letter follows the French sea
west is to the left in an across entry, so the island letter comes before Thailand's letter

parts.note: mer is French for sea
T is the international vehicle code for Thailand

explanation.surface: A desert island lies between French seas and the coast of Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert island' reads as one phrase; split it, as 'Desert' is the definition in the sense of what one deserves.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserts, as in just deserts, are what one deserves, and to merit is to deserve; the singular noun means worth.

clue.text: Plant's forbidden extract

parts.note: tref is the Yiddish word for food not kosher, forbidden under Jewish dietary law
an oil is an essence extracted from a plant

explanation.surface: A plant's essence is banned.
explanation.definitionFit: Trefoil is a clover-like plant with three-part leaves.

clue.text: Finish altering male tunic

indicators.note: altering a garment changes it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tailor completes the alterations on a man's tunic.
explanation.definitionFit: To culminate is to reach a final climax, so to come to an end.

clue.text: High-flier is acquiring estate, perhaps with title in Asia

indicators.note: something acquiring another takes it in, so the word 'is' wraps the car and title letters

parts.note: an estate is a type of car, the British name for a station wagon
U is a Burmese honorific title for a man, as in U Thant

explanation.surface: A high achiever owns a station wagon and holds an Asian title.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an estate is a car with a long rear load space, called a station wagon in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus flew too close to the sun on wings of wax, the original high-flier.

clue.text: See 9
Where tutte le strade lead — Cologne?

definitions.meaning: the Italian for 'all roads' lead to Rome, in Italian 'a Roma'
eau de cologne is a scent; the question mark flags it as one example

explanation.walkthrough: All roads lead to Rome; in Italian 'to Rome' is 'a Roma', which run together spells a word for a smell.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a pleasant smell, and cologne is a scented water worn for its fragrance.

clue.text: Eruption on mount Etna's summit featuring hot volcanic rock flowing west

parts.note: a rider on a mount, a horse, is said to be up
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: a summit is the top, so the first letter of the word
in an across entry, flowing west is going right to left, so the rock word is reversed

parts.note: lava is molten rock from a volcano, and the rock it cools into

explanation.surface: An eruption on Mount Etna sends hot lava flowing down its western side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eruption' sits naturally in the volcanic scene but is the definition in the sense of upheaval; 'featuring' just joins H and E.
explanation.definitionFit: An upheaval is a violent disturbance or sudden upthrust, an outbreak like an eruption.

clue.text: Thick-skinned creature getting potty after joint

indicators.note: after puts the potty word behind the joint word

parts.note: the hip is a joint of the body
po is a British informal word for a chamber pot

explanation.surface: An animal goes to the toilet after a hip operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick-skinned' suggests an insensitive person; here it describes the animal literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus has very thick hide, so it is literally a thick-skinned animal.

clue.text: Very probably contents'll go up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters are reversed
the contents of the words are the letters inside them

explanation.surface: Whatever is inside is very likely to burn.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are found inside 'Very probably' and read upwards; the whole clue also describes a funeral pyre, whose contents go up in flames.
explanation.definitionFit: A pyre is a heap of wood for burning a body, so its contents go up in smoke.

clue.text: Amphibian turning to salmon in Australian lake

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake, as on maps

indicators.note: turning round means facing back the other way, so the two words are read in reverse

parts.note: lox is smoked salmon

explanation.surface: An amphibian is changing into a salmon in an Australian lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' places the reversed TOLOX, XOLOT, inside A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: The axolotl is a Mexican salamander, an amphibian that keeps its larval gills into adulthood.

clue.text: Chicken perhaps like chickenfeed when grain kernel's replaced with regular portions of tofu

indicators.note: replaced with means one bit is swapped out for another

parts.note: chickenfeed means a trivial sum, so paltry

indicators.note: a kernel is the inner core, so the central letter of the word
regular portions are taken at even intervals, every other letter

explanation.surface: A chicken eats feed in which the grain has been swapped for tofu.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of 'grain' is A; in PALTRY it is replaced by OU, alternate letters of 'tofu'.
explanation.definitionFit: Poultry means domestic fowl, of which the chicken is the commonest example.

clue.text: Courier's head perhaps caught by flying bar stool — by which cowboy makes an entrance?

definitions.text: by which cowboy makes an entrance

indicators.note: something caught by another is held within it, so the editor sits inside the scrambled letters
a flying bar stool is hurtling through the air, so its letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the head of a newspaper such as the Courier is its editor, ED

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor is hit by a stool flung across a saloon bar as a cowboy walks in.
explanation.walkthrough: The Courier is a typical newspaper name; 'perhaps' marks it as an example of any paper whose head is the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy rides his horse, who lives in a stable, so the door into one is his entrance.

clue.text: Sexual licence to explore finished, with right approaching lead

indicators.note: approaching the lead means moving up towards the front, so the right letter shifts forward

parts.note: to feel something is to explore it by touch
something finished is over

explanation.surface: Permission to experiment sexually is finished, and the right thing is now in the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: FEEL plus OVER gives FEELOVER; moving R up to second place produces the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes sexual relations without commitment or marriage, which is licence in matters of sex.
